rv.q: This is a remarkable show that takes a cultural landmark from childhood as a springboard to confront what is so hard about moving into wisdom and purpose (there is a whole song about that), and it is perhaps the use of puppets that sneakily gets into your heart.
Music Theater Works certainly has another bonafide winner on its hands with this gleeful, gut-busting production of the 2004.
“Avenue Q” is that show with just the right amount of heart that makes you want to hug your friends a little tighter.

The show’s clever “Everyone’s a Little Bit Racist” tune has Frankenstein-ed into a real-world “lots of people are really racist” today. Yet the musical’s uplifting spirit remains untarnished, and every actor sings lovely tones and harmonies, accompanied by an excellent offstage, six-person orchestra.

Music Theater Works’s production, directed and choreographed by Christopher Pazdernik and with musical direction by Eugene Dizon, is an endearing and crowd-pleasing affair featuring a solid ensemble with supple voices, aided by cunning design work.
Music Theater Works is presenting a stellar production of this ( not for kids) musical.
The words are magic, the voices are fantastic, the costumes are perfect and the staging and choreography were just right.
Whitney Dottery is an absolute star as Gary Coleman. Her mugging and twinkle-eyed smile is the perfect tribute to the late child actor.

cn.t: Critics praise this energetic production of the Tony-winning musical as fresh and delightful despite being 20 years old, with its irreverent Sesame Street parody format and bawdy humor earning laughs, though it's decidedly not family-friendly.
